# Product Plan

Team: CTOS

## Purpose

An app that combines Wikipedia, YouTube, TikTok and other elements. The app is
an informational and social media app.

## Who are the users

Everyone and anyone, specifically anyone who wants a combination of the apps
listed above and their features too.

This app is made for people who want a combination of many features: video
sharing, chatting, watching, calling, group chats, communities, 3D avatar
models, and way more. People can turn off such features if wanted, just to fit
their expectations, and promote the successfulness of this app. People can turn
off and on features, if one or more does not fit expectations.

**Users:** all registered users on the app. Users are permanent accounts, unless
punishment for rule breaking is enacted.

**Guests:** all unregistered users. Guests are temporary accounts with 7 days,
pretty much a 1 week trial.

## Product description

This app combines the elements of Wikipedia, YouTube, TikTok, Snap and Discord.
You read informative topics, and you can also watch videos, text and call.
Wikipedia becomes Encyclopedia: topics you can read, with sources, photos and
videos to explain them, possibly with a quiz feature. YouTube becomes Media:
long form videos and content for engagement. TikTok becomes Media Shorts: short
form videos and content. Snap is merged with Discord into Chats: group, public
or private, message chat and call.

## Features

**In app messaging and calls:** Direct and private messages between 2 and 30
people, group chat, and calls and texts in the app.

**Avatar:** Design your own body, so people can express themselves.

**Shorts and videos:** Short form content and long form content, for
entertainment.

**Topics:** Reading informative topics like how to guides.

**Map:** Know where you should go and where others are.

**What you should get:** What you should get if you want the best item that fits
it, for example a car that is low mileage. Best deals.

**Streaks:** A streak is how much you have been messaging or calling someone,
for example 5 days.

**LIVEs:** Livestreams, for fun and entertainment.

**Data protection and encryption:** Protect your security and data, delete
messages, and so on.

**User support:** FAQs, what to do if you encounter bugs and issues, and reviews
about what could be done better.

**Bots:** To add more livelihood into your messages and communities, and for
user support.

**Turn features off and on:** Turn off and on the features you do not want, for
user autonomy.

**Advanced reports and moderation:** For safety.

**Algorithm sorting:** Sorting algorithm videos, best for engagement.

**Stickers and reaction images:** Express yourselves better.

**Public and private communities:** Build a public community messaging group
chat, Discord based, or a private one for you and friends.

**Quizzing:** Quiz others or yourself, for engagement and knowledge.

# CTOS user stories

Team: CTOS

Revised: 2026-09-17

These are the team's stories, tidied so that every one has a person, a want, a
reason, criteria that can be true or false, and a scenario a tester can run.
The narratives the team wrote are kept as the first paragraph of each story,
because they say what the feature is for better than any list could. The demo
at `/demo/period-7-ctos/` is built from these stories.

## Signing in

Users are permanent accounts. Guests are temporary accounts with a seven day
trial, so anyone can try the app before joining.

As a person opening CTOS, I want to sign in as a user or continue as a guest,
so that I can try the app before I commit to it.

  - Sign in asks for a username and nothing else
  - Continue as guest needs nothing and shows how many trial days are left
  - A guest sees a banner saying the trial ends in 7 days and can join at any time
  - After signing in I land on Media

  Given I press Continue as guest
  When I look at the top of the screen
  Then it says Guest, 7 days left, and offers Join

  Given I am a guest
  When I press Join and type a username
  Then the banner goes away and my username is on my profile

## Shorts and videos

Shorts are short form content: videos 75 seconds or less. Videos are long form.
Both are found in Media.

As a user, I want to post a video and watch what others posted, so that I can
share with the world and be entertained.

  - Media lists every post, newest first, marked Short or Video
  - Posting asks for a title, a link and whether it is a Short or a Video
  - A post with no title or no link is refused with a message that says which
  - The Shorts chip shows only Shorts, the Videos chip only Videos
  - I can like a post and the count goes up by one

  Given I am on Media
  When I press Create, fill in a title and a link, pick Short and press Post
  Then my post is at the top of Media marked Short

  Given I am on Media
  When I tap the Shorts chip
  Then only posts marked Short are listed

## Topics

# A new direction for CTOS

Written with the team, 25 September. A proposal, not a replacement: your own
plan and stories are exactly where you left them, and nothing here becomes
your plan until you say so.

## What we noticed

Your plan lists 17 features and names five apps: Wikipedia, YouTube, TikTok,
Snap and Discord. Read quickly, it looks like "all of social media in one app".

Read slowly, it is something else. Messaging, calls, group chats, stickers,
reactions, avatars, communities, streaks, user support: almost every feature
is about **talking to people and being understood by them**. The five apps
were never the point. They were the clearest examples of how people
communicate, and the plan was reaching for that.

So here is the app we think is underneath it.

## The idea

**A school chat app where everyone writes in their own language and reads in
theirs.**

A student who has just moved here and is still learning English opens the app
in Mandarin or Spanish. A classmate writes "want to sit with us at lunch?" in
English and it arrives in Mandarin. The answer goes back in English. Nobody
has to wait until their English is good enough to make a friend.

Around the chat sit the things a new student needs in their first weeks: the
phrases you need in the hallway, guides to how this school works, a map with
room names in your language, and a buddy who has done it before.

## Why this is a stronger app

- **You can name the user.** "Everyone and anyone" is nobody in particular. A
  student in their first months at a school where they do not speak the
  language yet is a real person with a real problem.
- **Every feature has a reason.** Streaks are no longer just for fun: they keep
  a new student talking every day, which is how a language is learned.
- **It is small enough to build.** Fourteen features, all about one thing,
  instead of five apps.
- **Almost none of your work is thrown away.** See the table below.

## Where your features went

| Your feature | In the new plan | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| In app messaging and calls | **Translated messaging**, **Group chats in any language**, **Calls with live captions** | Every message is translated for whoever reads it. Your 2 to 30 person limit is kept. |
| Stickers and reaction images | **Stickers and reactions** | Now the way to say something when you have no words yet. |
| Avatar | **Avatar** | Unchanged. Showing who you are without writing a paragraph about it. |
| Streaks | **Streaks** | A streak with your buddy is practice every day. |
| Topics (Encyclopedia) | **School guides** | Short guides to how this school works, in every language. |
| Quizzing | **Practice** | Quizzes on the phrases you actually need. Your grade bands still work. |
| Map | **School map** | Rooms labelled in your language, and a button to ask the way. |
| Public and private communities | **Buddies and clubs** | A buddy who speaks your language, and clubs for each language. |
| Turn features off and on | **Turn features off and on** | Unchanged. |
| User support, reports and moderation, data protection | **Safety and support** | Report, block, and help in your own language. |
| Users and Guests | **Choose your language** | Picking a language comes first. Guests are kept for now, see question 3. |
| Shorts and videos, LIVEs | Left out | Nothing about them helps somebody be understood. |
| What you should get, Algorithm sorting | Left out | Same reason. |
| Bots | Later, maybe | A bot that explains a word you did not understand could be good. Write a story for it if you want it. |

"Left out" means left out of this proposal. Your original plan still has
them, and putting one back is your decision.

## Three things this app has to get right

1. **Translation is sometimes wrong.** Every translated message has a
   **Show original** button, and a new student can ask "Did I say that
   right?" without it being embarrassing. An app that hides its mistakes will
   get somebody laughed at.
2. **The users are children.** Only people at the same school can message
   each other, and anyone can report or block from inside a chat. No
   strangers, no public profiles.
3. **Which language you speak is personal.** It is not on anyone's profile
   and the app never uses it to sort or search for people. The only place it
   appears is the small "translated from" note on a message, because the
   reader needs to know a translation happened.

## Questions for the team

1. **Is this your app?** If any part of it is not what you meant, change it.
   This is a draft for you to edit, not a correction.
2. **Should teachers be in it?** A student who can message the counsellor in
   their own language is useful. It also changes who can see what.
3. **Do guests still make sense?** For an app at one school, accounts could
   come from the school instead. Your call.
4. **What is it called?** The plan still has no name, so the demo says CTOS.
   Some starting points, if they help: *Bridge*, *Hello Hallway*, *Say It*,
   *Common Ground*. Yours will be better.

## The pages in this folder

- **Product Plan**: the reframed plan, rewritten around the idea above, with
  your sections in your order.
- **Reframed user stories**: fourteen stories, one per feature. Where you
  already wrote a narrative, it is kept and adjusted rather than replaced.

There is a working demo of all fourteen at
[/demo/period-7-ctos/](/demo/period-7-ctos/). Open it on a phone and pick a
language.

## When you say yes

Tell your teacher. They will move these two files into your folder in place of
the old ones (keeping the old ones as `original-product-plan.md` and
`original-user-stories.md`), and your prototype, build cards, test plan and
gap guide are rebuilt from them with one command. Until then those pages still
show your original plan, which is on purpose.

# Product Plan

Team: CTOS

Proposal, 25 September. Not adopted yet: the team's own plan is
`product-plan.md` one folder up.

## Purpose

Students who have just moved to a school in a new country, and are still
learning its language, often cannot talk to the people around them. They
understand more than they can say, they miss what is going on, and making a
friend has to wait until their English is good enough.

This app lets everyone at a school write in their own language and read in
theirs, in real time, so a new student can talk to classmates from their first
day, and learn the language by using it.

## Who are the users

**New students:** students in their first months at the school who are still
learning English. They use the app in their own language: Mandarin, Spanish,
or any other it supports.

**Classmates:** students who already speak English, and who want to talk to a
new student without a shared language getting in the way. Many of them will
use it to practise a language too.

**Buddies:** students who volunteer to help a new student in their first weeks.
Often they speak the same first language and arrived a year or two earlier.

Everyone is a student at the same school. Nobody from outside the school can
message a student.

## Product description

A chat app for one school. Every message is translated for whoever reads it,
so a group chat can have a Mandarin speaker, a Spanish speaker and an English
speaker all talking at once, each reading in their own language. The original
is always one tap away, because translation is sometimes wrong.

Around the chat are the things a new student needs in their first weeks:
quick phrases for the hallway, short guides to how the school works, a school
map in their language, practice on the phrases they use most, and a buddy.

Stickers, reactions and avatars are there because they say things without
needing words. Streaks are there because talking every day is how a language
is learned.

## Features

**Choose your language:** The first screen asks which language you speak, in
that language. The whole app, not just the messages, switches to it.

**Translated messaging:** Direct messages between two people. Everyone writes
in their own language and reads in theirs. Every translated message has Show
original.

**Group chats in any language:** Group chats of 2 to 30 people, where every
member reads every message in their own language.

**Calls with live captions:** A voice call where what the other person says
appears as captions in your language.

**Quick phrases:** A set of ready-made phrases for school, like "Can you say
that more slowly?" or "Where is room 204?", in every language. Tap one and it
goes into your message.

**Stickers and reactions:** Say something without words. The sticker tray and
reactions work the same in every language.

**Streaks:** Days in a row you have talked to somebody. A streak with your
buddy is practice every day.

**School guides:** Short guides to how the school works: lunch, the bus, hall
passes, what a word like "tardy" means. Every guide is in every language, and
can be read aloud.

**Practice:** Quizzes on the phrases you need, in the language you are
learning. Scored with the team's grade bands.

**School map:** A map of the school with every room named in your language and
in English, and a button to ask somebody the way.

**Buddies and clubs:** Get matched with a buddy, and join a club for your
language or for the language you are learning.

**Avatar:** Build a model of yourself, so people can see who you are.

**Turn features off and on:** Turn off the features you do not use.

**Safety and support:** Report or block anyone from inside a chat, and find
help in your own language.

# CTOS: build architecture

Team: CTOS. Tool: Anvil.

## The buildable slice

You listed 17 features and, when this page was first written, had 2 user
stories. On 10 September that became 12. It is still worth being direct about
the plan: it describes Wikipedia, YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat and Discord
combined, and those five companies employ tens of thousands of engineers
between them.

That is not a reason to feel bad. Ambition is where good products start. But
building starts with choosing, so here is the choice.

**In the slice, in this order:**

1. Sign in
2. Post a video (title, link, and whether it is a Short or a Video)
3. The feed
4. Build a quiz
5. Take a quiz

**Stubbed, and why:**

- **In app messaging and calls.** A narrative and no scenario, so there is no
  finish line to build to yet. This is the one your cards suggest writing first.
- **Avatar.** A narrative and no scenario. A 3D model is also outside what Anvil
  can draw; the first version would be a picture chosen from a list.
- **Topics.** A narrative with no "so that" and no scenario.
- **Map.** A narrative with no "so that" and no scenario, and it needs an
  outside service. The first version of a map is a list of places.
- **Streaks.** A narrative and no scenario. It also needs messaging to exist
  first, because a streak counts messages.
- **User support.** A narrative and no scenario.
- **Turn features off and on.** A narrative and no scenario.
- **Stickers and reaction images.** A narrative and no scenario, and it needs
  messaging to exist first.
- **Public and private communities.** A narrative and no scenario, and it needs
  messaging to exist first.
- **What you should get, LIVEs, Data protection and encryption, Bots, Advanced
  reports and moderation, Algorithm sorting.** No story at all.

**The way anything on that list gets off it** is one story with acceptance
criteria and a Given, When, Then. Write it, and it gets a card and a place on
this page. Sorting by newest, which you called algorithm sorting, is already in
the feed.

**Pick your app's name while you are at it.** Your plan says "App Name :" and
leaves it blank, so this prototype is titled after your team.

## Screens to create

| Form name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SignIn` | Sign in or sign up |
| `Feed` | Every posted video, newest first |
| `PostVideo` | Add a video |
| `QuizBuilder` | Make a quiz |
| `TakeQuiz` | Answer a quiz and get a score |

## Components, with the exact names to use

**SignIn:** `btn_sign_in`

**Feed:** `rp_videos` with `lbl_video_title`, `lbl_kind`, `lbl_posted_by`;
`btn_post`, `btn_quizzes`

**PostVideo:** `txt_title`, `txt_link`, `dd_kind` (DropDown: Short, Video),
`btn_upload`, `lbl_error`

**QuizBuilder:** `txt_question`, `txt_answer`, `btn_add_question`,
`rp_questions` with `lbl_question_line`; `btn_finish`

**TakeQuiz:** `lbl_question`, `txt_answer`, `btn_submit`, `lbl_score`

## Data tables

- **videos**: `title`, `link`, `kind` (Short or Video), `posted_by`, `posted`
  (date and time)
- **quizzes**: `name`, `made_by`, `is_public` (true or false)
- **questions**: `quiz` (text), `question`, `answer`

## How each feature gets built

### Feature 1: Sign in
Patterns: **12**, **4**.

### Feature 2: Post a video
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **13**, **6**, **7**, **5**, **4**.

Your story says "I see a box that says upload video here". Uploading a video
file is heavy. Start with a title and a link to a video that already exists,
which is what most of the internet actually does.

Your newer stories draw a line at 75 seconds: at or under is a Short, over is a
Video. The app cannot measure a link, so the person posting picks one from
`dd_kind` (Pattern 13) and it is saved in the `kind` column with the rest.

### Feature 3: The feed
Patterns: **8**, **11**, **9**.

Newest first: `tables.order_by("posted", ascending=False)`. Your plan calls this
"algorithm sorting". Sorting by newest is an algorithm. You have built it.

Each row shows `kind` in `lbl_kind`, so the feed says Short or Video beside the
title. Showing only Shorts is one filter away, and a story away.

### Feature 4: Build a quiz
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **6**, **7**, then **8**, **9** to show the questions
added so far.

Your quiz story is unusually well specified: you wrote out the grade bands, the
plus and minus buttons, and public versus private. Build the adding of questions
first, then the rest.

### Feature 5: Take a quiz and get a score
Patterns: **8**, **3**, **1**, **6**, **10**.

Show a question, compare the typed answer to the stored one, count the right
ones, show the score against your grade bands at the end.

**Your grade bands are your acceptance criteria.** 96 to 100 is Awesome. Test it
by getting them all right and all wrong.

## What to do when you are stuck

1. Do not know what the app should do, go to your build card.
2. Do not know how to write it, go to the Pattern Book.
3. Do not know what fills the blank, come back here.

# CTOS: design brief

Everything on this page came out of your own build architecture. Nobody typed it for you, and nobody will keep it up to date by hand: change the architecture and this page changes with it.

That is the point. Your builders have already agreed on the name of every button and every label in CTOS, by CTOS. If your Figma layers use those names, the person writing the code can look at your design and find their own component in it. If they do not, they are guessing.

The rules for how to set the file up are on **[Designing for Anvil](/build/figma.html)**. This page is only your team's part.

Starting from nothing? **[Start your design with AI](/build/figma-ai.html)** turns your user story into the prompt and then lists the four things every AI design gets wrong. And the page your builder uses to match what you drew is **[Make Anvil look like your Figma](/build/look.html)**: read it before you draw a gradient.

Would rather be walked through it? **[Design, step by step](walkthrough.html)** shows one step at a time in these exact names, checks what you typed against this page, and has the helper on every step. It remembers where your team got to.

## Your frames

One frame per screen, named exactly like this. Not "Home v2", not "final home". This name.

| Frame name | What happens on it |
|---|---|
| `SignIn` | Sign in or sign up |
| `Feed` | Every posted video, newest first |
| `PostVideo` | Add a video |
| `QuizBuilder` | Make a quiz |
| `TakeQuiz` | Answer a quiz and get a score |

## What goes on each frame

The left column is the **layer name to use in Figma**. Copy it exactly, underscores and all.

### SignIn

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `btn_sign_in` | Button |  |

### Feed

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `rp_videos` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_video_title` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_kind` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_posted_by` | Label |  |
| `btn_post` | Button |  |
| `btn_quizzes` | Button |  |

> **`rp_videos` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_video_title`, `lbl_kind` and `lbl_posted_by`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

### PostVideo

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `txt_title` | TextBox |  |
| `txt_link` | TextBox |  |
| `dd_kind` | DropDown | Your architecture says: Short, Video. |
| `btn_upload` | Button |  |
| `lbl_error` | Label |  |

### QuizBuilder

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `txt_question` | TextBox |  |
| `txt_answer` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_add_question` | Button |  |
| `rp_questions` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_question_line` | Label |  |
| `btn_finish` | Button |  |

> **`rp_questions` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_question_line`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

### TakeQuiz

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_question` | Label |  |
| `txt_answer` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_submit` | Button |  |
| `lbl_score` | Label |  |

## Draw the bad day too

Every screen has three states and designers almost always draw one of them. The happy one. Your builder then has to invent the other two while writing code, at speed, and it shows.

**Empty.** Nothing has been added yet.

You have a repeating list on Feed and QuizBuilder. On the first day of using this app, that list has nothing in it. What does the screen say? "Nothing here yet" is a design decision, and it is yours.

**Wrong.** Somebody typed something the app will not accept.

Your architecture already has an error label: `lbl_error` on PostVideo. It starts invisible and appears when something is refused. Right now nobody has designed what it looks like. Red text? A box? Where on the screen? Decide it, because otherwise it will be default grey in the middle of nowhere.

**Full.** Somebody has used this for a month.

Long names, a hundred rows, a review that is a paragraph rather than four words. Designs break at the edges, and the edges are where real people live.

## The pieces you are working with

These are the components your team is actually using. Anvil gives you a fixed set of them, which is a real constraint on the design and not a small one. Figma will happily let you draw something nobody on your team can build.

| Component | You can change | You cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Button | The text, the icon, the text colour, the background colour, and the size. | Give it a custom shape, a gradient, or a hover animation. |
| RepeatingPanel | Everything inside the one row. | Make row three look different from row one. |
| Label | The words, size, colour, bold or italic, alignment, and an icon beside it. | Make it a box with a border and a background of its own. |
| TextBox | The placeholder text, the width, and whether it hides what is typed. | Put an icon or a button inside the box itself. |
| DropDown | The list of choices and the width. | Style the open list, or put pictures in the choices. |

## Before you hand it over

- [ ] One frame per screen, named exactly as in the table above
- [ ] Every layer name matches a name in this page, spelled the same way
- [ ] Repeating lists are designed as one row, not several
- [ ] The empty state and the error state are drawn, not just the good one
- [ ] Real words from your own app, not lorem ipsum and not "Button 1"
- [ ] Your colours written down as hex codes, because that is what gets typed into Anvil

Then show it to whoever is writing the code and ask them one question: **can you find every one of your components in this?** If the answer is no, you have found the gap before it cost anybody a period of work, which is the entire job.

# PC BROS

Team: The Dream Team

Draft: true

## Purpose

Gaming PCs are built for people with money. A student who saves up for months
still ends up choosing between a machine that is too expensive and one that will
not run the games they actually play, and nobody explains which of the two they
are buying.

PC BROS is for **kids like us**: pick your own parts, watch the price add up as
you go, and get a machine that is exactly the one you designed, hand built, with
your name on it if you want it there.

## Who are the users

**Students who game:** They know what games they want to play and have a
number in their head they cannot go over. They do not know what a GPU is called
or which one matters, and every site that could tell them is written for
somebody twice their age. They want to choose the parts themselves rather than
be sold a box.

**Whoever actually pays:** A parent, a grandparent, somebody at a birthday. They
are not buying the PC, they are approving it. They want to see what it costs
before they say yes, know what is in it, and be sure the thing that arrives is
the thing that was agreed.

**The PC BROS workshop:** Us. Somebody has to read the order, build that exact
machine, and say when it has shipped. We are a real part of how this works and
the app does not do anything for us yet, which is a hole worth knowing about
rather than one to be embarrassed by.

## Product description

PC BROS is a custom PC shop for students and young people. You choose your own
parts on our site, the price updates as you pick each one, and when you are
happy you place the order and we build it by hand.

Every machine is built to that exact order, with an engraving on the metal if
you want one, so what turns up is yours rather than whatever was in the
warehouse. You can watch your order's progress from ordered to built to shipped.
And if you would rather do it in person, our store is a real place you can walk
into and build it on the bench with us.

## Features

**Build your own PC:** Choose a CPU, graphics card, memory, storage and case
from what we stock, one at a time.

**The price as you go:** The running total updates every time you pick a part,
so you always know where you are against your budget before you commit to
anything.

**Order your build:** Check the whole build on one screen, add an engraving and
a delivery address, and place the order. An order missing a part or an address
is refused rather than half saved.

**Track your order:** See every order you have placed, newest first, and what
stage it has reached.

**Find our store:** Where the shop is, when it is open, and what happens if you
come in and build it on the bench instead of online.

# PC BROS: build architecture

Team: The Dream Team. Tool: Anvil.

## The buildable slice

Your app is small, and that is an advantage. You can finish it.

**In the slice, in this order:**

1. Pick your parts
2. See the price add up
3. Place the order
4. See your orders

**Stubbed, and why:**

- **Actually building and shipping the PC.** That happens in a workshop, not in
  Anvil. Everything the customer touches is buildable.
- **Custom engravings.** A text box on the order. Add it once the four above
  work.

- **Find our store.** New in your plan, and it is one screen with an address, an
  opening time and a sentence on it. Genuinely easy, and it needs a user story
  before it is worth building, because right now nobody has said what somebody
  is trying to do when they open it.

- **The workshop screen.** Your `orders` table has a `status` column and nothing
  in your app ever changes it. Somebody has to read an order, build that machine
  and mark it shipped, and that somebody is you. It is the same three patterns
  as Feature 4 with a button on the end. Park it until the customer side works,
  then notice that you already know how to build it.

**Two things to settle.**

**The product name is decided, for now.** Your plan called the product both "The
dream team" and "PC BROS". Your teacher has been calling the project PC Bros, so
these pages use **PC BROS** as the product and **The Dream Team** as the team.
Say if that is the wrong way round, because it is on every page you have.

**Your only story is written from the company's point of view**: "As a PC
company I want to make money so I can be rich." That is a business goal, not a
user story. Your customer wants a good PC at a price they can afford. Card 1
rewrites it that way, and it changes what you build.

## Screens to create

| Form name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Builder` | Choose each part |
| `Review` | The full build and the total price |
| `MyOrders` | Orders you have placed |

## Components, with the exact names to use

**Builder:** `dd_cpu`, `dd_gpu`, `dd_ram`, `dd_storage`, `dd_case` (DropDowns);
`lbl_running_total`; `btn_review`

**Review:** `lbl_build_summary`, `lbl_total`, `txt_engraving`, `txt_address`,
`btn_place_order`, `lbl_error`

**MyOrders:** `rp_orders` with `lbl_order_line`, `lbl_order_status`

## Data tables

- **parts**: `category`, `name`, `price` (number)
- **orders**: `customer`, `build`, `total` (number), `engraving`, `address`, `status`, `placed` (date and time)

## How each feature gets built

### Feature 1: Pick your parts
Patterns: **8**, **13**.

Fill each dropdown from the parts table, one category each:
`app_tables.parts.search(category="CPU")`.

### Feature 2: The price adds up
Patterns: **13**, **3**, and a little arithmetic.

Read each dropdown's `selected_value`, add the prices, put the total in
`lbl_running_total`. Do it every time a dropdown changes, using the dropdown's
`change` event instead of a button click. That is Pattern 1 with a different
event name, which is a useful thing to discover.

### Feature 3: Place the order
Patterns: **6**, **7**, **5**, **4**.

Refuse an order with no address, or with a part left unchosen.

### Feature 4: See your orders
Patterns: **8**, **11**, **9**.

## What to do when you are stuck

1. Do not know what the app should do, go to your build card.
2. Do not know how to write it, go to the Pattern Book.
3. Do not know what fills the blank, come back here.

# PC BROS: design brief

Everything on this page came out of your own build architecture. Nobody typed it for you, and nobody will keep it up to date by hand: change the architecture and this page changes with it.

That is the point. Your builders have already agreed on the name of every button and every label in PC BROS, by The Dream Team. If your Figma layers use those names, the person writing the code can look at your design and find their own component in it. If they do not, they are guessing.

The rules for how to set the file up are on **[Designing for Anvil](/build/figma.html)**. This page is only your team's part.

Starting from nothing? **[Start your design with AI](/build/figma-ai.html)** turns your user story into the prompt and then lists the four things every AI design gets wrong. And the page your builder uses to match what you drew is **[Make Anvil look like your Figma](/build/look.html)**: read it before you draw a gradient.

Would rather be walked through it? **[Design, step by step](walkthrough.html)** shows one step at a time in these exact names, checks what you typed against this page, and has the helper on every step. It remembers where your team got to.

## Your frames

One frame per screen, named exactly like this. Not "Home v2", not "final home". This name.

| Frame name | What happens on it |
|---|---|
| `Builder` | Choose each part |
| `Review` | The full build and the total price |
| `MyOrders` | Orders you have placed |

## What goes on each frame

The left column is the **layer name to use in Figma**. Copy it exactly, underscores and all.

### Builder

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `dd_cpu` | DropDown |  |
| `dd_gpu` | DropDown |  |
| `dd_ram` | DropDown |  |
| `dd_storage` | DropDown |  |
| `dd_case` | DropDown |  |
| `lbl_running_total` | Label |  |
| `btn_review` | Button |  |

### Review

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_build_summary` | Label |  |
| `lbl_total` | Label |  |
| `txt_engraving` | TextBox |  |
| `txt_address` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_place_order` | Button |  |
| `lbl_error` | Label |  |

### MyOrders

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `rp_orders` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_order_line` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_order_status` | Label |  |

> **`rp_orders` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_order_line` and `lbl_order_status`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

## Draw the bad day too

Every screen has three states and designers almost always draw one of them. The happy one. Your builder then has to invent the other two while writing code, at speed, and it shows.

**Empty.** Nothing has been added yet.

You have a repeating list on MyOrders. On the first day of using this app, that list has nothing in it. What does the screen say? "Nothing here yet" is a design decision, and it is yours.

**Wrong.** Somebody typed something the app will not accept.

Your architecture already has an error label: `lbl_error` on Review. It starts invisible and appears when something is refused. Right now nobody has designed what it looks like. Red text? A box? Where on the screen? Decide it, because otherwise it will be default grey in the middle of nowhere.

**Full.** Somebody has used this for a month.

Long names, a hundred rows, a review that is a paragraph rather than four words. Designs break at the edges, and the edges are where real people live.

## The pieces you are working with

These are the components your team is actually using. Anvil gives you a fixed set of them, which is a real constraint on the design and not a small one. Figma will happily let you draw something nobody on your team can build.

| Component | You can change | You cannot |
|---|---|---|
| DropDown | The list of choices and the width. | Style the open list, or put pictures in the choices. |
| Label | The words, size, colour, bold or italic, alignment, and an icon beside it. | Make it a box with a border and a background of its own. |
| Button | The text, the icon, the text colour, the background colour, and the size. | Give it a custom shape, a gradient, or a hover animation. |
| TextBox | The placeholder text, the width, and whether it hides what is typed. | Put an icon or a button inside the box itself. |
| RepeatingPanel | Everything inside the one row. | Make row three look different from row one. |

## Before you hand it over

- [ ] One frame per screen, named exactly as in the table above
- [ ] Every layer name matches a name in this page, spelled the same way
- [ ] Repeating lists are designed as one row, not several
- [ ] The empty state and the error state are drawn, not just the good one
- [ ] Real words from your own app, not lorem ipsum and not "Button 1"
- [ ] Your colours written down as hex codes, because that is what gets typed into Anvil

Then show it to whoever is writing the code and ask them one question: **can you find every one of your components in this?** If the answer is no, you have found the gap before it cost anybody a period of work, which is the entire job.

# GAMEHACK

Team: GameHack

## Purpose

An app that can help you get past a difficult part in a game, or make the game
easier and more fun. It helps kids get past difficult parts of the game.

## Who are the users

**Gamers:** People who play video games in general, and people who want to know
how to beat a level or make it easier.

**Kids:** Players who get stuck and want to finish the game faster.

**Modders:** People interested in learning more about how a game works.

## Product description

An app that has many features to help get past difficult parts in games. It can
give people video game tips and help them beat specific hard parts of video
games using an AI that calculates that part of the game.

## Features

**AI:** An AI that calculates methods and tutorials for specific hard parts, so
people can get easy access to the parts they might be stuck on.

**Tutorials:** Showing how to do something, in this case teaching how to beat a
game or a level, so users can accomplish a goal.

**Tips:** Video game tips for a specific part of a game.

**Maps:** Maps for finding your way around a game.

**Cheat codes:** Codes that make a game easier.

**Mods:** Modifications that change how a game plays.

# GAMEHACK: build architecture

Team: GameHack. Tool: Anvil.

## The buildable slice

**In the slice, in this order:**

1. Browse tutorials by game
2. Search for a game
3. Add a tutorial
4. Ask the helper

**Stubbed, and why:**

- **An AI that understands games.** Your helper answers from a table of question
  and answer pairs that you write. That is honest and it works. Building a real
  game-aware AI is a research project.
- **Maps, cheat codes and mods.** No user story for any of them, so there is
  nothing to build from. They are also all the same shape as a tutorial: a title,
  a game, a link. Once tutorials work, adding a type column gets you all three
  at once, which is worth noticing before you build three separate screens.

**One thing to settle first.** One of you wrote "There are no scenarios in our
App, it just gives you links to video game tutorials". The other two wrote
stories about an AI that calculates methods. Those are two different products.
Decide which one GAMEHACK is before you build, because it changes everything
below.

## Screens to create

| Form name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Games` | Every game with tutorials |
| `Tutorials` | Tutorials for one game |
| `AddTutorial` | Submit a tutorial link |
| `Helper` | Ask a question, get an answer |

## Components, with the exact names to use

**Games:** `txt_search`, `btn_search`, `rp_games` with `lbl_game_name`,
`lbl_tutorial_count`

**Tutorials:** `lbl_game_name`, `rp_tutorials` with `lbl_tutorial_title`,
`lbl_tutorial_link`; `btn_add`

**AddTutorial:** `dd_game`, `txt_title`, `txt_link`, `btn_submit`, `lbl_error`

**Helper:** `txt_question`, `btn_ask`, `lbl_answer`

## Data tables

- **games**: `name`
- **tutorials**: `game` (text), `title`, `link`, `added_by`
- **helper_answers**: `keyword`, `answer`

## How each feature gets built

### Feature 1: Browse tutorials by game
Patterns: **8**, **9**, then **1**, **4** to open one game.

### Feature 2: Search
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **8**, **9**.

Search the table with what was typed:
`app_tables.games.search(name=typed_in)`. That only finds exact matches, which
is a good problem to hit. Solving it properly comes later.

### Feature 3: Add a tutorial
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **13**, **6**, **7**, **5**.

Your criteria say a user must be able to follow the tutorials you have linked.
The check you can actually build is that the link is not empty.

### Feature 4: Ask the helper
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **8**, **6**, **3**.

Look for a keyword from the question in your answers table. If nothing matches,
say so honestly rather than guessing. "I do not know that one yet" is a better
answer than a wrong one, and knowing that is worth more than the feature.

## What to do when you are stuck

1. Do not know what the app should do, go to your build card.
2. Do not know how to write it, go to the Pattern Book.
3. Do not know what fills the blank, come back here.

# GAMEHACK: design brief

Everything on this page came out of your own build architecture. Nobody typed it for you, and nobody will keep it up to date by hand: change the architecture and this page changes with it.

That is the point. Your builders have already agreed on the name of every button and every label in GAMEHACK, by GameHack. If your Figma layers use those names, the person writing the code can look at your design and find their own component in it. If they do not, they are guessing.

The rules for how to set the file up are on **[Designing for Anvil](/build/figma.html)**. This page is only your team's part.

Starting from nothing? **[Start your design with AI](/build/figma-ai.html)** turns your user story into the prompt and then lists the four things every AI design gets wrong. And the page your builder uses to match what you drew is **[Make Anvil look like your Figma](/build/look.html)**: read it before you draw a gradient.

Would rather be walked through it? **[Design, step by step](walkthrough.html)** shows one step at a time in these exact names, checks what you typed against this page, and has the helper on every step. It remembers where your team got to.

## Your frames

One frame per screen, named exactly like this. Not "Home v2", not "final home". This name.

| Frame name | What happens on it |
|---|---|
| `Games` | Every game with tutorials |
| `Tutorials` | Tutorials for one game |
| `AddTutorial` | Submit a tutorial link |
| `Helper` | Ask a question, get an answer |

## What goes on each frame

The left column is the **layer name to use in Figma**. Copy it exactly, underscores and all.

### Games

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `txt_search` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_search` | Button |  |
| `rp_games` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_game_name` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_tutorial_count` | Label |  |

> **`rp_games` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_game_name` and `lbl_tutorial_count`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

### Tutorials

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_game_name` | Label |  |
| `rp_tutorials` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_tutorial_title` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_tutorial_link` | Label |  |
| `btn_add` | Button |  |

> **`rp_tutorials` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_tutorial_title` and `lbl_tutorial_link`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

### AddTutorial

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `dd_game` | DropDown |  |
| `txt_title` | TextBox |  |
| `txt_link` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_submit` | Button |  |
| `lbl_error` | Label |  |

### Helper

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `txt_question` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_ask` | Button |  |
| `lbl_answer` | Label |  |

## Draw the bad day too

Every screen has three states and designers almost always draw one of them. The happy one. Your builder then has to invent the other two while writing code, at speed, and it shows.

**Empty.** Nothing has been added yet.

You have a repeating list on Games and Tutorials. On the first day of using this app, that list has nothing in it. What does the screen say? "Nothing here yet" is a design decision, and it is yours.

**Wrong.** Somebody typed something the app will not accept.

Your architecture already has an error label: `lbl_error` on AddTutorial. It starts invisible and appears when something is refused. Right now nobody has designed what it looks like. Red text? A box? Where on the screen? Decide it, because otherwise it will be default grey in the middle of nowhere.

**Full.** Somebody has used this for a month.

Long names, a hundred rows, a review that is a paragraph rather than four words. Designs break at the edges, and the edges are where real people live.

## The pieces you are working with

These are the components your team is actually using. Anvil gives you a fixed set of them, which is a real constraint on the design and not a small one. Figma will happily let you draw something nobody on your team can build.

| Component | You can change | You cannot |
|---|---|---|
| TextBox | The placeholder text, the width, and whether it hides what is typed. | Put an icon or a button inside the box itself. |
| Button | The text, the icon, the text colour, the background colour, and the size. | Give it a custom shape, a gradient, or a hover animation. |
| RepeatingPanel | Everything inside the one row. | Make row three look different from row one. |
| Label | The words, size, colour, bold or italic, alignment, and an icon beside it. | Make it a box with a border and a background of its own. |
| DropDown | The list of choices and the width. | Style the open list, or put pictures in the choices. |

## Before you hand it over

- [ ] One frame per screen, named exactly as in the table above
- [ ] Every layer name matches a name in this page, spelled the same way
- [ ] Repeating lists are designed as one row, not several
- [ ] The empty state and the error state are drawn, not just the good one
- [ ] Real words from your own app, not lorem ipsum and not "Button 1"
- [ ] Your colours written down as hex codes, because that is what gets typed into Anvil

Then show it to whoever is writing the code and ask them one question: **can you find every one of your components in this?** If the answer is no, you have found the gap before it cost anybody a period of work, which is the entire job.

# Your Template

Product name: Math Bros Inc.
Team: Team Orangutan

## Purpose

To teach people math so they can get smarter.

## Who are the users

People who need help with math, which is basically everyone, because you can
always improve.

## Product description

An app that teaches math. Different courses on different subjects of math, for
example addition and subtraction, trigonometry, 2 digit multiplication,
factoring any kind of polynomial of higher degrees, and graph theory, with
videos and guides on how to do it.

## Features

**Video:** A video in the course to help visual learners understand math, so it
teaches people math and they get smarter.

**Quiz:** A quiz at the end of the course, so it helps you get more familiar
with the mathematical subjects and get more knowledge.

**Placement test:** It sorts users based on skill level, so the experience is
not too complicated or too easy.

**AI assistant:** You put in a mathematical equation and it gives the answer,
like a calculator for everything. It also gives you the steps to solve it, so
you learn more about problems you do not know.

**Secret age groups:** After the placement test, users get assigned to an age
group. They do not get told. This way everyone gets a personalized experience
with the appropriate level of challenge.

**Leaderboard:** A leaderboard for the most XP earned, because competition
encourages players to keep playing.

**Racing game against AI:** A racing game against an AI slightly more advanced
than your level, so students work harder to beat it.

**Dictionary:** A dictionary for many mathematical subjects and theorems, a
handy reference for students confused about a word.

**Secret mode:** Accessed by pressing a key combination. A prank where
calculations are off by one, so 1 plus 1 is 3. No benefits, just funny.

# Math Bros Inc. user stories

Team: Team Orangutan

Revised: 2026-09-17

These are the team's stories, tidied so that every one has a person, a want, a
reason, criteria that can be true or false, and a scenario a tester can run.
The two racing stories became one. The demo at `/demo/period-7-orangutan/`
is built from them and from the team's Figma design.

## Signing in

As a student, I want to pick a username, so that my points and my place on the
leaderboard are mine.

  - The home screen has a Get Started button
  - Sign in asks for a username and nothing else
  - An empty username is refused with a message that says so
  - I can change my username later and the leaderboard shows the new one

  Given I open Math Bros for the first time
  When I press Get Started and type a username
  Then I see the home screen with my name on it

  Given I have changed my username to GeorgeDeng
  When I open the leaderboard
  Then my row says GeorgeDeng

## Placement test

As a new student, I want to take a placement test, so that the questions I get
are not too hard or too easy.

  - The test has ten questions that get harder as they go
  - I can type an answer or pick from choices, depending on the question
  - After each answer I am told whether it was right
  - At the end I see how many I got right and how many wrong
  - I can retake the test and my level changes if my score does

  Given I am a new student on the home screen
  When I press Start placement test
  Then question 1 opens with a box to type my answer

  Given I have answered all ten questions
  When the last one is marked
  Then I see my score out of ten and Practice is unlocked

## Secret age groups

As a student, I want the math to fit my skill level without being told what
group I am in, so that nobody feels labelled.

  - The placement test sets my level and the app never shows it as a number or an age
  - Getting three practice questions right in a row moves me up a level
  - Getting two wrong in a row moves me down a level
  - The level dots on the practice screen fill up and empty as I move, and that is the only sign

  Given my placement score put me at level 2
  When I get three practice questions right in a row
  Then the next question is a level 3 question and one more dot is filled

  Given I am on any screen
  When I look for my age group
  Then it is not written anywhere

## Practice

As a student, I want to practise a subject with questions at my level, so that
I get better at it and earn points.

  - There are six subjects: Algebra, Geometry, Calculus, Statistics, Trigonometry and Number Theory
  - Each question is typed or multiple choice and I am told right away if I was right
  - A right answer is worth 10 points
  - A typed answer is not marked wrong for capital letters or spaces
  - The screen shows how many I got right and wrong this session

  Given I choose Algebra
  When I answer a question correctly
  Then I see Correct, my points go up by 10 and the next question appears

  Given I type "X + 8" and the answer is "x + 8"
  When I submit
  Then it is marked correct

## Video

As a student, I want to watch a lesson video in a course, so that I can see
the material explained before I try it.

  - Each course has a lesson with a name and a length
  - I can play and pause it
  - I can switch to 2x speed
  - I can skip to a part of the lesson by tapping the timeline
  - When the lesson ends I am offered the quiz

  Given I open the Algebra course
  When I press Play
  Then the lesson starts from the beginning and the time counts up

  Given the lesson is playing
  When I press 2x
  Then the time counts up twice as fast

## Quiz

As a student, I want to take a quiz at the end of a course, so that I can see
if I learned the material.

  - The quiz has five questions from that course
  - I can type an answer or pick from choices, depending on the question
  - At the end it shows how many were right and how many wrong
  - A quiz score of 4 or 5 earns 50 points

  Given I have finished the Algebra lesson
  When I press Take the quiz
  Then question 1 of 5 opens

  Given I got 4 of 5 right
  When the quiz ends
  Then I see 4 right, 1 wrong and 50 points added

## AI assistant

As a student who is stuck on a problem, I want to type it in and get the answer
with the steps, so that I learn how to do it and not just what the answer is.

  - I can type an equation like 2x + 3 = 11 or a sum like 48 divided by 6
  - The assistant shows the answer and the steps to get there
  - I can press Explain it simpler and get the same steps in plainer words
  - If it cannot solve what I typed, it says so and suggests what it can do

  Given I type 2x + 3 = 11
  When I press Solve
  Then I see x = 4 and the three steps that got there

  Given the steps are too hard
  When I press Explain it simpler
  Then the same answer appears with shorter, plainer steps

## Race against AI

As a student who is bored of plain practice, I want to race a bot at math
questions, so that I work harder to beat it.

  - I can choose a subject and a difficulty (easy, normal, extreme)
  - The bot moves forward on its own, faster on harder difficulties
  - I move forward one space for every right answer, and a wrong answer says so
  - First to the finish wins, and beating the bot earns 100 points

  Given I pick Algebra and easy
  When I answer five questions right before the bot finishes
  Then I win and 100 points are added

  Given I pick extreme
  When the race starts
  Then the bot moves faster than it does on easy

## Math dictionary

As a student who does not understand a word in a problem, I want to look it
up, so that I can carry on with the problem.

  - The dictionary is in alphabetical order
  - Typing in the search box narrows the list as I type
  - Each word has a plain definition and an example
  - A word that is not there says so and offers the closest match

  Given I type "prime"
  When the list narrows
  Then I see Prime number with its definition

  Given I type "zorb"
  When nothing matches
  Then the screen says no match and suggests a nearby word

## Leaderboard

As a student, I want to see who has the most points, so that I have a reason
to keep practising.

  - The leaderboard lists everyone from most points to least
  - My row is highlighted and shows my rank
  - Points on the leaderboard are the same points I earned in practice, quizzes and races
  - The board tells me how many points I need to move up one place

  Given I have just earned 10 points
  When I open the leaderboard
  Then my row has moved up if those points passed someone

  Given I am not in first place
  When I look at my row
  Then it says how many more points would move me up one

## Secret mode

As a student who likes a joke, I want a hidden mode where calculations are off
by one, so that I can prank a friend.

  - Tapping the logo five times turns secret mode on and shows a small banner
  - In secret mode the AI assistant's answers are one too big
  - Tapping the logo five more times turns it off
  - Secret mode never changes points or the leaderboard

  Given I tap the logo five times
  When I ask the assistant what 1 + 1 is
  Then it says 3 and the banner says secret mode is on

  Given secret mode is on
  When I answer practice questions
  Then my points are counted normally

# Team Orangutan: build architecture

Team: Team Orangutan. Tool: Anvil.

## The buildable slice

You wrote the most complete set of stories in the class: five stories, most with
real Given, When and Then lines. That earns you a bigger slice than anyone else.

**In the slice, in this order:**

1. Placement test
2. Course list, filtered by level
3. Watch a video
4. Take a quiz and get a score
5. Leaderboard
6. Secret mode

**Stubbed, and why:**

- **A real AI assistant that solves equations.** Your assistant answers from a
  table of worked examples you write. The step by step explanation your story
  asks for is exactly what goes in that table, so writing them is the feature.
- **The racing game against an AI.** No story, and it is a whole game.

**Give your app a name.** Your plan never does, so this prototype is titled
after your team, and your app deserves better.

## Screens to create

| Form name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Placement` | The test that sets your level |
| `Courses` | Courses for your level |
| `Video` | Watch a course video |
| `Quiz` | Answer questions, get a score |
| `Leaderboard` | Most XP first |

## Components, with the exact names to use

**Placement:** `lbl_question`, `txt_answer`, `btn_submit`, `lbl_progress`

**Courses:** `rp_courses` with `lbl_course_name`, `lbl_course_topic`;
`btn_leaderboard`

**Video:** `lbl_video_title`, `lbl_video_link`, `lbl_length`, `btn_take_quiz`

**Quiz:** `lbl_question`, `txt_answer`, `btn_submit_answer`, `lbl_score`

**Leaderboard:** `rp_ranks` with `lbl_rank_name`, `lbl_rank_xp`

## Data tables

- **users_progress**: `user`, `display_name` (text), `level` (number), `xp` (number)
- **courses**: `name`, `topic`, `level` (number), `video_link`, `video_length`
- **questions**: `course` (text), `question`, `answer`

## How each feature gets built

### Feature 1: Placement test
Patterns: **8**, **3**, **1**, **2**, **6**, then **7** or **10** to save the
level.

Ask a few questions, count the right answers, save a level number. Your "secret
age groups" story says the level is never shown to the user, so save it and
simply never put it in a label. **That is the whole feature.** Some of the best
features are the ones nobody sees.

### Feature 2: Course list for your level
Patterns: **8**, **6**, **9**.

Look up this user's level, then search courses for that level:
`app_tables.courses.search(level=my_level)`.

### Feature 3: Watch a video
Patterns: **1**, **4**, **3**.

Your story asks for pause, 2x speed and skipping. Those belong to the video
player itself, not to your code. Show the link and the length. Recognising which
parts you build and which parts the player already does is real engineering.

### Feature 4: Quiz and score
Patterns: **8**, **3**, **1**, **6**, **10**.

Count right and wrong, show both, add XP for right answers.

### Feature 5: Leaderboard
Patterns: **8**, **11**, **9**.

`tables.order_by("xp", ascending=False)`. This is the single cleanest use of
Pattern 11 in the class.

Your leaderboard story, now written, adds two things. **Names**: `lbl_rank_name`
shows `display_name`, not the email, and when somebody changes their username
to GeorgeDeng it is this column that changes, so the board changes with it.
**Movement**: a student who just earned XP should see themselves higher. That is
already true, because the board is worked out fresh from the table every time it
opens; there is nothing to update. Notice that you get it for free because
nothing is stored twice.

### Feature 6: Secret mode
Patterns: **1**, **6**, **14**.

Your prank where 1 plus 1 shows 3. A key combination is fiddly, so start with a
hidden button in a corner. Build this last, as a reward.

## Your Figma has moved past this page

Your team built the app in Figma Make and named it **Math Bros Inc.**, and the
design has screens this page does not: a **Home** with a hero and six
subjects, a **Practice** list, a **SubjectQuiz** that gets harder as you get
questions right, and a results screen for the placement test. It has no video
screen. Your Anvil app follows the Figma, so this page is behind it, and it
gets brought up to date once the Anvil app is in the repository to read from.

Until then, the [project code guide](code-guide-README.html) is the page that
matches: it is your Figma read back as Anvil components, with every colour,
font and word from the design, and it is about the **look**. Your code is
yours; that guide is for making it look like the thing you drew.

## What to do when you are stuck

1. Do not know what the app should do, go to your build card.
2. Do not know how to write it, go to the Pattern Book.
3. Do not know what fills the blank, come back here.

# Math Bros Inc.: design brief

Everything on this page came out of your own build architecture. Nobody typed it for you, and nobody will keep it up to date by hand: change the architecture and this page changes with it.

That is the point. Your builders have already agreed on the name of every button and every label in Math Bros Inc., by Team Orangutan. If your Figma layers use those names, the person writing the code can look at your design and find their own component in it. If they do not, they are guessing.

The rules for how to set the file up are on **[Designing for Anvil](/build/figma.html)**. This page is only your team's part.

Starting from nothing? **[Start your design with AI](/build/figma-ai.html)** turns your user story into the prompt and then lists the four things every AI design gets wrong. And the page your builder uses to match what you drew is **[Make Anvil look like your Figma](/build/look.html)**: read it before you draw a gradient.

Would rather be walked through it? **[Design, step by step](walkthrough.html)** shows one step at a time in these exact names, checks what you typed against this page, and has the helper on every step. It remembers where your team got to.

## Your frames

One frame per screen, named exactly like this. Not "Home v2", not "final home". This name.

| Frame name | What happens on it |
|---|---|
| `Placement` | The test that sets your level |
| `Courses` | Courses for your level |
| `Video` | Watch a course video |
| `Quiz` | Answer questions, get a score |
| `Leaderboard` | Most XP first |

## What goes on each frame

The left column is the **layer name to use in Figma**. Copy it exactly, underscores and all.

### Placement

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_question` | Label |  |
| `txt_answer` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_submit` | Button |  |
| `lbl_progress` | Label |  |

### Courses

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `rp_courses` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_course_name` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_course_topic` | Label |  |
| `btn_leaderboard` | Button |  |

> **`rp_courses` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_course_name` and `lbl_course_topic`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

### Video

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_video_title` | Label |  |
| `lbl_video_link` | Label |  |
| `lbl_length` | Label |  |
| `btn_take_quiz` | Button |  |

### Quiz

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `lbl_question` | Label |  |
| `txt_answer` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_submit_answer` | Button |  |
| `lbl_score` | Label |  |

### Leaderboard

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `rp_ranks` | RepeatingPanel |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_rank_name` | Label |  |
|   ↳ `lbl_rank_xp` | Label |  |

> **`rp_ranks` repeats.** Design **one** row containing `lbl_rank_name` and `lbl_rank_xp`, and Anvil stamps out a copy of it for every row of data. If you draw four rows that look different from each other, only the first one is real. Draw the one row, then say how many you expect to see.

## Draw the bad day too

Every screen has three states and designers almost always draw one of them. The happy one. Your builder then has to invent the other two while writing code, at speed, and it shows.

**Empty.** Nothing has been added yet.

You have a repeating list on Courses and Leaderboard. On the first day of using this app, that list has nothing in it. What does the screen say? "Nothing here yet" is a design decision, and it is yours.

**Wrong.** Somebody typed something the app will not accept.

No screen in your architecture has a place to show an error yet. That is worth raising with your team: every screen where someone types something needs somewhere to say no.

**Full.** Somebody has used this for a month.

Long names, a hundred rows, a review that is a paragraph rather than four words. Designs break at the edges, and the edges are where real people live.

## The pieces you are working with

These are the components your team is actually using. Anvil gives you a fixed set of them, which is a real constraint on the design and not a small one. Figma will happily let you draw something nobody on your team can build.

| Component | You can change | You cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Label | The words, size, colour, bold or italic, alignment, and an icon beside it. | Make it a box with a border and a background of its own. |
| TextBox | The placeholder text, the width, and whether it hides what is typed. | Put an icon or a button inside the box itself. |
| Button | The text, the icon, the text colour, the background colour, and the size. | Give it a custom shape, a gradient, or a hover animation. |
| RepeatingPanel | Everything inside the one row. | Make row three look different from row one. |

## Before you hand it over

- [ ] One frame per screen, named exactly as in the table above
- [ ] Every layer name matches a name in this page, spelled the same way
- [ ] Repeating lists are designed as one row, not several
- [ ] The empty state and the error state are drawn, not just the good one
- [ ] Real words from your own app, not lorem ipsum and not "Button 1"
- [ ] Your colours written down as hex codes, because that is what gets typed into Anvil

Then show it to whoever is writing the code and ask them one question: **can you find every one of your components in this?** If the answer is no, you have found the gap before it cost anybody a period of work, which is the entire job.

# Daily

Team: The Lions

## Purpose

An app that encourages you to be active while doing everyday activities. It
tells you the weather so you can know if there are good conditions for physical
activities, and tells you about nearby areas with the nutrition your body needs
after being active.

## Who are the users

**Unorganized people who need reminders:** People who need a daily routine.

**People trying to build good habits:** People who want to create good habits
and keep them.

## Product description

A simplistic app for people who need a daily routine and people who want to
create good habits. It is very compatible with all types of disabilities, and it
has many features including dieting control, it can make a workout routine, and
you have an AI helper.

## Features

**Daily routine:** A simple routine to follow, so people stay organized.

**AI helper:** Chat with an AI about productivity, diets and general tips.

**Nutrition planner:** Dieting control and nutritional planning.

**Workout routine:** It can make a workout routine for you.

**Weather:** Tells you the weather so you know if conditions are good for being
active outside.

**Share your routine:** Share your routine with other people.

**Rewards:** Rewards for keeping up with your habits.

# Daily user stories

Team: The Lions

Revised: 2026-09-17

## Daily routine

As a user, I want to stay organized and gain good habits, so that I will be a
better person overall.

  - User should gain good habits
  - User should stay organized
  - User should know what they missed
  Given I am a user who is trying to build good habits
  When I use the app to make good habits
  Then it will work properly and actually help me
  Given I am trying to keep track of my schedule
  When I open the app to check my schedule
  Then I can see what I have done and what I have to do
  Given I am trying to lose weight
  When I use the app to get an eating routine
  Then I will get an eating routine optimized to help me lose weight

## Nutrition planner and scanner

As a person wanting to get more fit and change their diet, I want to know what
foods will be the most beneficial for my goals, so that I can grow and be the
best version of myself.

  - Person should be able to set goals and get food-related outputs
  - Scanner should be able to tell the person what they will get out of the food
  - Scanner should adjust for the person's goal
  Given someone wants to eat more protein to help build muscle
  When they scan a food label
  Then it will tell them if it is high in protein to help them with their goals
  Given someone wants to lose weight
  When they scan a food label
  Then it will tell them if the food is healthy or not

## AI helper

As a person looking to get stronger, I want to know whether lots of weight and
few reps or little weight and lots of reps is better, and other general tips, so
that I can maximize the amount of muscle I grow and be the best version of
myself.

  - Person needs to be able to ask a lot of questions
  - AI needs to constantly respond correctly
  - AI needs to be helpful based on different situations
  - AI should be programmed to think of general things that humans like
  Given someone wants strength tips
  When they ask the AI about weights that are helpful for their goals
  Then the AI will respond with good helpful answers and tips
  Given someone does not know where to start
  When they ask the AI about how to build up to a pushup
  Then the AI will tell them helpful advice like planks

## Timer user story

As a person trying to time how long I want to do a workout., I want to be able to have a working timer, so that I can accurately time my workouts.

  - A timer that can be accurate
  - The timer should count down in seconds

  Given I am trying to time someone
  When I start the timer
  Then it will count down

## Daily Calender

As a someone, who wants to have planned workout and diet schedules, I want to be able to see what my workouts or meals are for the day or month, so that I will be able to get more fit.

  - A calender that shows small workout or diet plans for the month as well as the day in more specific detail

  Given I want to know what's going on today for excersise
  When I look at my Daily calender
  Then I will see that I have soccer practice at 5:30

  Given I am wondering what I should be eating today
  When I check my Daily calender
  Then it will show me that I need to eat more vegetables today in order to fit my weight loss goal

## Login

As a person trying to log back into Daily, I want to log in to Daily, so that I will be able to access it and use the app.

  - For this to work properly you must click the login button and get a text sent to your phone number so you can log in

  Given I want to log in to Daily
  When I click the login button
  Then I should be given a code to my phone

## The profile.

As a person wanting to customize the way you are seen on Daily, I want to be able to change my photo/name, so that people can see my personality on Daily.

  - You will be able to click on your profile and see it
  - You will be able to customize your photo and name

  Given I want to customize my photo
  When I click on my profile
  Then I will be able to click the photo and change it

  Given I want to upload a photo for my profile picture
  When I clicked my photo
  Then daily will be able to access your photo album and you will be able to select a photo

## Streak Counter

As a Student, I want to have a streak, so that I can flex on my friends.

  - An area that shows my streak
  - Increase everyday they log in
  - Resets every time that don't log in for the day

  Given I am a student
  When I open the app to check my streak
  Then it will show my streak so I can flex on my friends

  Given I am an old man
  When I forget to open my app
  Then it will show a restore streak for $5.99 notification

# Daily: build architecture

Team: The Lions. Tool: Anvil.

## The buildable slice

**In the slice, in this order:**

1. Sign in
2. Add a habit
3. Tick off today
4. Streaks
5. The helper

**Stubbed, and why:**

- **Live weather.** Needs an outside service. Pick today's conditions from a
  dropdown instead, which changes nothing else about your app.
- **A real AI helper.** Answers come from a table of question and answer pairs
  you write. Your fitness story asks about heavy weight with few reps versus
  light weight with many. Write that answer yourselves. It is a better answer
  than a generic AI would give, because you know what your users are asking.
- **Sharing routines, rewards.** No stories, so nothing to build from.
  Rewards are close to streaks, so they may come almost free.
- **The food scanner.** Your nutrition story now has a person, criteria and two
  scenarios, and its card is Card 6. Reading a food label through a camera
  needs an outside service, so it is not in the slice yet. Ask your teacher
  which feature number it gets, and what stands in for the camera.

## Screens to create

| Form name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SignIn` | Sign in or sign up |
| `Today` | Your habits for today, with tick boxes |
| `AddHabit` | Create a new habit |
| `Helper` | Ask a question, get an answer |

## Components, with the exact names to use

**SignIn:** `btn_sign_in`

**Today:** `dd_weather` (DropDown), `rp_habits` with `lbl_habit_name`,
`chk_done`, `lbl_streak`; `btn_add_habit`, `btn_helper`

**AddHabit:** `txt_habit_name`, `dd_how_often`, `btn_save_habit`, `lbl_error`

**Helper:** `txt_question`, `btn_ask`, `lbl_answer`

## Data tables

- **habits**: `user`, `name`, `how_often`, `streak` (number)
- **completions**: `user`, `habit` (text), `done_on` (date)
- **helper_answers**: `keyword`, `answer`

## How each feature gets built

### Feature 1: Sign in
Patterns: **12**, **4**.

### Feature 2: Add a habit
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **13**, **6**, **7**, **5**.

Refuse an empty habit name.

### Feature 3: Tick off today
Patterns: **8**, **9**, then **1**, **7** when a box is ticked.

The tick box lives inside the repeating panel's item template, so its handler
reads `self.item` to know which habit it belongs to. This is the trickiest part
of your app and it is worth taking slowly.

### Feature 4: Streaks
Patterns: **8**, **6**, **10**, **3**.

If today's completion follows yesterday's, add one to the streak. If a day was
missed, set it back to 1. This is the most interesting logic in your app and it
is where your product actually helps somebody.

### Feature 5: The helper
Patterns: **1**, **2**, **8**, **6**, **3**.

## What to do when you are stuck

1. Do not know what the app should do, go to your build card.
2. Do not know how to write it, go to the Pattern Book.
3. Do not know what fills the blank, come back here.

| `lbl_error` | Label |  |

### Helper

| Layer name | Anvil component | Anything special |
|---|---|---|
| `txt_question` | TextBox |  |
| `btn_ask` | Button |  |
| `lbl_answer` | Label |  |

## Draw the bad day too

Every screen has three states and designers almost always draw one of them. The happy one. Your builder then has to invent the other two while writing code, at speed, and it shows.

**Empty.** Nothing has been added yet.

You have a repeating list on Today. On the first day of using this app, that list has nothing in it. What does the screen say? "Nothing here yet" is a design decision, and it is yours.

**Wrong.** Somebody typed something the app will not accept.

Your architecture already has an error label: `lbl_error` on AddHabit. It starts invisible and appears when something is refused. Right now nobody has designed what it looks like. Red text? A box? Where on the screen? Decide it, because otherwise it will be default grey in the middle of nowhere.

**Full.** Somebody has used this for a month.

Long names, a hundred rows, a review that is a paragraph rather than four words. Designs break at the edges, and the edges are where real people live.

## The pieces you are working with

These are the components your team is actually using. Anvil gives you a fixed set of them, which is a real constraint on the design and not a small one. Figma will happily let you draw something nobody on your team can build.

| Component | You can change | You cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Button | The text, the icon, the text colour, the background colour, and the size. | Give it a custom shape, a gradient, or a hover animation. |
| DropDown | The list of choices and the width. | Style the open list, or put pictures in the choices. |
| RepeatingPanel | Everything inside the one row. | Make row three look different from row one. |
| Label | The words, size, colour, bold or italic, alignment, and an icon beside it. | Make it a box with a border and a background of its own. |
| CheckBox | The label text and the colour. | Turn it into a toggle switch. |
| TextBox | The placeholder text, the width, and whether it hides what is typed. | Put an icon or a button inside the box itself. |

## Before you hand it over

- [ ] One frame per screen, named exactly as in the table above
- [ ] Every layer name matches a name in this page, spelled the same way
- [ ] Repeating lists are designed as one row, not several
- [ ] The empty state and the error state are drawn, not just the good one
- [ ] Real words from your own app, not lorem ipsum and not "Button 1"
- [ ] Your colours written down as hex codes, because that is what gets typed into Anvil

Then show it to whoever is writing the code and ask them one question: **can you find every one of your components in this?** If the answer is no, you have found the gap before it cost anybody a period of work, which is the entire job.

# Bus Buddy

Team: Sample Team

This is a worked example, written the way a real team would write it, including
the mistakes. One feature has no user story and one story has no "so that", so
the coach notes in the generated prototype have something true to say.

## Purpose

Students at our school wait outside for buses that are late, early, or already
gone, and nobody tells them which. Parents call the front office to ask where
the bus is, and the office cannot answer either. Bus Buddy tells everybody the
same thing at the same time so nobody is standing in the rain guessing.

## Who are the users

**Students:** They want to know how many minutes until their bus reaches their
stop, and whether it is worth leaving class early to catch it. They are on
phones, they are in a hurry, and they will not read anything long.

**Parents:** They want to know their kid got on the bus and when the bus will
reach their neighborhood. They mostly want to stop calling the school.

**Bus drivers:** They want to report a delay once and have it reach everyone,
instead of answering the same question forty times.

**Front office staff:** They want to see every route at once so they can answer
a phone call in ten seconds instead of ten minutes.

## Product description

Bus Buddy is a phone app that shows where school buses are and when they will
arrive. Students set their bus number and their stop, and the app shows a
countdown. Drivers can report a delay in two taps, and every rider on that route
sees it immediately. The front office gets a board with every route on it.

## Features

**Bus tracker:** Shows the countdown to your bus reaching your stop, and where
the bus is right now.

**Delay alerts:** Drivers report a delay, and every rider on that route is told
right away with the reason and the new time.

**My stop setup:** Lets a rider choose their bus number and their stop once, so
the app knows what to show them.

**Route board:** A screen for the front office showing every route and its
status at the same time.

**Ride history:** A record of which buses a student rode and when. We have not
written a story for this one yet.

# Bus Buddy user stories

Team: Sample Team

## Bus tracker

As a student, I want to see how many minutes until my bus reaches my stop, so
that I stop standing outside guessing.

  Given I have set my bus number and my stop
  When I open the app
  Then I see a countdown in minutes and where the bus is on the route

As a parent, I want to see where my child's bus is, so that I know when to walk
down to the stop.

  Given my child has shared their bus number with me
  When I select their route
  Then I see the same countdown my child sees

## Delay alerts

As a bus driver, I want to report a delay in two taps, so that I am not
answering the same question forty times.

  Given I am on my route and running late
  When I tap report a delay and choose a reason
  Then every rider on my route is told the new arrival time

As a student, I want to be told when my bus is late, so that I do not leave
class early for nothing.

  Given my bus has been reported late
  When the delay is posted
  Then I see the new time and the reason on my home screen

## My stop setup

As a student, I want to choose my bus number and my stop once, so that the app
knows what to show me every morning.

  Given I am opening the app for the first time
  When I enter my bus number
  Then the app saves it and shows me my stop list

  Given I have picked my bus
  When I select my stop from the list
  Then the app remembers it and takes me to the tracker

## Route board

As front office staff, I want to see every route on one screen.

  Given a parent is on the phone asking about a bus
  When I open the route board
  Then I see every route with its status and its next stop
